mainTopic: Backing out of accepting unfit judges (timing, הלכה, קנין), and a new משנה on who is disqualified from testifying, starting with the dice player.
overview: The amud opens by defending רבא's rule that רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue only about "אתן לך" (I will give you), not about "מחול לך" (it is forgiven to you). The גמרא shows that both cases in the משנה are "אתן לך" cases, and that each is needed: one relies on outsiders, the other on the opponent himself. Next, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue whether the dispute is before or after גמר דין. Using רבא's ruling, the גמרא concludes that for רבי יוחנן the dispute is only after the verdict. Several versions of a letter then give the final הלכה like the חכמים, and שמואל rules that after a קנין no one can back out. A new משנה lists people who are פסול to testify, such as dice players and lenders with interest. רבי יהודה adds that they are פסול only if this is their only job. The גמרא brings two reasons why a dice player is פסול: אסמכתא (רמי בר חמא) or not doing useful work (רב ששת). It then challenges רמי בר חמא from רבי יהודה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't the second case of the משנה a forgiving case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the סיפא is about a defendant who would swear and be free, so the claimant who offers the vow is really saying "מחול לך". That would go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the משנה talking about people who take an oath and then don't pay? In that case it is like saying "it is forgiven to you", and still רבי מאיר says he can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא from the second case of the משנה. It suggests that this case is really a "מחול לך" situation, where רבא said nobody can back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the defendant swears and is then free from paying. If the claimant tells him "just make a vow instead", the claimant is giving up his money claim, which is like "מחול לך". Yet רבי מאיר lets him back out, and that contradicts רבא's claim that everyone agrees in a "מחול לך" case.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it…?" A way of suggesting a reading that leads to a challenge
Those who swear and so don't pay (the defendant swears and goes free)
"It is forgiven to you". Giving up money you are owed

steps.confusionAlert: The "oath" here belongs to the defendant, not the claimant. The claimant is the one offering to accept a vow, and that is why it counts as forgiving.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו בְּאוֹתָן הַנִּשְׁבָּעִין וְלֹא מְשַׁלְּמִין,
phrases.english: Is it not about those who swear and do not pay,
which is like saying "it is forgiven to you"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בְּאוֹתָן הַנִּשְׁבָּעִין וְלֹא מְשַׁלְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's earlier rule (from before this section) using the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that in a "מחול לך" case everyone agrees one cannot back out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the סיפא is a case where the defendant swears and goes free, then accepting his vow is "מחול לך". Yet רבי מאיר allows backing out, so the argument does apply to "מחול לך".

steps.title: No, it is a case where the claimant swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is about a claimant who would swear and collect. The defendant who offers the vow is saying "אתן לך".
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about people who take an oath and collect, so it is like saying "I will give you".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the second case differently. It is an "אתן לך" case, where רבא agrees there is an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In some cases the claimant swears and then collects his money. If the defendant says "just vow by your life and I'll pay", he is offering to give money, which is "אתן לך". So רבי מאיר letting him back out fits רבא perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who swear and collect (the claimant swears and gets paid)
"I will give you". Promising to pay

phrases.english: No, it is about those who swear and collect,
which is like saying "I will give you".

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּאוֹתָן הַנִּשְׁבָּעִין וְנוֹטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by switching which side owes the oath.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא): a different kind of oath situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is about a defendant who swears and goes free, which is "מחול לך".
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is about a claimant who swears and collects, which is "אתן לך". It fits רבא.

steps.title: But the first case already taught "I will give you"
steps.stepSummary: If the סיפא is also an "אתן לך" case, it seems to repeat the רישא, which already taught that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part of the משנה already taught this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If both cases are "אתן לך", why would the משנה say the same thing twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the רישא (accepting my father or your father as judge) is already about someone who agrees to pay based on an unreliable source. Making the סיפא the same kind of case seems to make it extra, and a משנה does not repeat itself for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it already taught it". A challenge that something is repeated
The first part of a משנה

phrases.english: But the first part already taught it!
phrases.notes: The first part is the case of accepting "my father" or "your father" as a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 for making the משנה repeat itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the סיפא as an "אתן לך" case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רישא already teaches the "אתן לך" law, then a second "אתן לך" case in the סיפא adds nothing.

steps.title: One case depends on others, the other on the opponent himself
steps.stepSummary: The two cases are different. In the רישא he relies on outsiders (the fathers). In the סיפא he relies on his opponent's own word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught a case where he makes it depend on other people, and it taught a case where he makes it depend on the other person's own decision.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both cases are needed, because each one teaches something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא the outcome rests on third parties, the fathers. In the סיפא it rests on the opponent himself, who is an interested party. You might have thought the law changes when you trust your opponent directly, so the משנה teaches both, and רבא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Hangs it on; makes the outcome depend on
On the decision of others (outside people)
On his own decision (the opponent himself)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule survives: the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is about "אתן לך". The משנה's two cases are both "אתן לך" cases. One trusts outsiders and one trusts the opponent himself.

phrases.english: It taught a case where he relies on the decision of others,
and it taught a case where he relies on his own decision.
phrases.notes: "His own" means the opponent's own word, his vow by his life.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים, וּתְנָא תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition challenge of step 3 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart: each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא and סיפא are both "אתן לך" cases, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא depends on outsiders and the סיפא depends on the opponent himself, so both are needed.

steps.title: Why the first case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the משנה had only taught the case of relying on outsiders. We might think רבי מאיר lets him back out only there, because he never really expected to lose. But when he relies on his opponent's own word, רבי מאיר might agree with חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to teach both cases. If the משנה had only taught the case where he relies on the opinion of others, we would say that only there רבי מאיר lets him back out. That is because he never fully made up his mind to hand over the money. He was thinking: 'Who says they will rule in the other side's favor?' But where he relies on his opponent's own word, we might say רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its answer from Step 4. It shows that the רישא alone would not teach us what the סיפא teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא he relies on outsiders, like the fathers. So he can tell himself they might rule for him, and he never truly committed to paying. In the סיפא he relies on his opponent, who will surely swear in his own favor. So he knew he would probably lose, and that sounds like a real commitment. Without the סיפא, we might think רבי מאיר agrees he cannot back out there.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary. Both cases are needed.
Making the outcome depend on other people's decision
Fully decides to transfer ownership
Making the outcome depend on the opponent's own decision

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'עצמו' does not mean the person backing out. It means the other side, the claimant, whose oath he is relying on.

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if it had taught
one who relies on the decision of others,
in this case רבי מאיר says
that he can back out,
because he did not fully decide to transfer the money,
since he says: 'Who says they will rule in his favor?'
phrases.notes: He was thinking to himself that the outsiders might rule for him, not for the other side.

phrases.english: but one who relies on the decision of the man himself,
phrases.notes: 'The man himself' means the opponent, who will be the one swearing.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי תְּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands Step 4's answer by showing what the סיפא adds beyond the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the רישא alone, we might think רבי מאיר lets him back out only when he relies on outsiders.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא teaches that רבי מאיר lets him back out even when he relies on his opponent's word.

steps.title: Why the second case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the משנה had only taught the case of relying on the opponent. We might think חכמים say he cannot back out only there. In the case of outsiders, they might agree with רבי מאיר. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had only taught us this case, we would say that only here חכמים say he cannot back out. But in that other case, we might say חכמים agree with רבי מאיר. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא from the other direction. It shows that the סיפא alone would not teach us what the רישא teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, his commitment looks strong, so of course חכמים would say he is bound. In the רישא, his commitment looks weak, so we might think even חכמים let him back out. The רישא teaches that חכמים hold him bound even there.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us
They agree

steps.whatToRemember: Each case teaches something new. The רישא, relying on outsiders, shows how far חכמים go. The סיפא, relying on the opponent, shows how far רבי מאיר goes.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the סיפא, where he relies on his opponent's oath.

phrases.english: in this case the Rabbis say he cannot back out,
but in that other case

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: I would say the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Meir.
So it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא from the opposite side and closes the question from Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the סיפא alone, we might think חכמים agree with רבי מאיר when he relies on outsiders.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא teaches that חכמים hold him bound even when he relies on outsiders.

steps.title: Is the argument before or after the verdict?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the מחלוקת is only before גמר דין. After the verdict, everyone agrees he cannot back out. רבי יוחנן says the מחלוקת is after גמר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The argument is before the verdict. But after the verdict, everyone agrees he cannot back out. And רבי יוחנן said: The argument is after the verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. Two אמוראים argue about when the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר lets him back out only before the ruling is given. Once the ruling is given, everyone agrees he is stuck. רבי יוחנן says that even after the ruling, רבי מאיר still lets him back out.

keyTerms.meaning: Dispute
The final verdict
Everyone agrees
To back out of his agreement

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the timing for the whole מחלוקת and leads straight into the question in the next step.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The dispute is before the verdict,
phrases.notes: This is the argument between רבי מאיר and the Rabbis in our משנה about backing out.

phrases.english: but after the verdict,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: all agree he cannot back out.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is after the verdict.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַחְלוֹקֶת לִפְנֵי גְּמַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the timing of the משנה's מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: the מחלוקת is only before the verdict, and afterward everyone agrees he cannot back out. רבי יוחנן: the מחלוקת is after the verdict.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן hold about before the verdict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand רבי יוחנן. Maybe the מחלוקת is only after גמר דין, and before it everyone agrees he can back out. Or maybe the מחלוקת applies in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the argument only after the verdict, while before the verdict everyone agrees he can back out? Or maybe the argument applies both here and there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to clarify רבי יוחנן's view. It is setting up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the מחלוקת is after גמר דין. That could mean the argument is only then, and before the verdict even חכמים let him back out. Or it could mean the argument is in both cases, and he mentioned 'after' only to show how far רבי מאיר goes.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Or perhaps
Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: They asked:
Is the dispute only after the verdict,
but before the verdict
all agree he can back out?
Or perhaps:
the dispute applies both in this case and in that case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְאַחַר גְּמַר דִּין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 7 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוחנן, does the מחלוקת also apply before גמר דין, or does everyone agree then that he can back out?

steps.title: רבא's ruling on backing out before and after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling to settle how to read רבי יוחנן: before גמר דין one can back out, after גמר דין one cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבא said: if someone accepted a relative or a disqualified person, he can back out before the verdict. After the verdict he cannot back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רבא to help answer the question from Step 8. The next step will show how this ruling proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the case into two times. Before the verdict, backing out is allowed. After the verdict, it is not. This split will be the key to understanding רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who normally cannot be a judge or witness
Someone disqualified from being a judge or witness
To back out, to take back what he agreed to
The final verdict

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rava says:
If one accepted upon himself a relative or a disqualified person,
phrases.notes: He agreed to let this person judge or testify in his case, even though normally they couldn't.

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי גְּמַר דִּין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: before the verdict, he can back out;

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר גְּמַר דִּין אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: after the verdict, he cannot back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question raised in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: How to understand רבי יוחנן's view of when the מחלוקת applies
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling: before גמר דין he can back out, after גמר דין he cannot

steps.title: רבא fits only one way of reading רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן holds the מחלוקת is only after גמר דין, then רבא rules like רבי יוחנן according to חכמים. If the מחלוקת is in both cases, רבא matches no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say the מחלוקת is after the verdict and before the verdict everyone agrees he can back out. Then רבא is ruling like רבי יוחנן, following חכמים. But if you say the מחלוקת is in both cases, whose view is רבא following?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both possible readings of רבי יוחנן against רבא's ruling. Only one reading fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Reading 1, before the verdict everyone agrees he can back out, and after it חכמים say he cannot. That is exactly רבא's ruling. In Reading 2, רבי מאיר would let him back out even after the verdict, and חכמים would stop him even before it. So רבא's split would match neither side.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say: this reading fits
Everyone agrees
According to the view of the חכמים
Both in this case and in that case
Like whom? Whose view does this follow?

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not ruling like רבי מאיר. In the reading that works, רבא's ruling that he can back out before the verdict is something everyone agrees to. His ruling that he cannot back out after the verdict follows חכמים.

phrases.english: It works well if you say:
the dispute is after the verdict,
but before the verdict
everyone agrees he can back out,
then Rava is ruling like Rabbi Yochanan
and according to the Rabbis.
But if you say:
the dispute is both in this case and in that case,
then whose view is Rava ruling like?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבא's ruling from Step 9 decides between the two readings in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: Reading 1 of רבי יוחנן: the מחלוקת is only after גמר דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's split ruling matches Reading 1 and fits no one under Reading 2

steps.title: The dispute is only after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that according to רבי יוחנן, the מחלוקת is only after גמר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, can't we learn from this that the מחלוקת is after the verdict? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof and accepts it. רבי יוחנן's מחלוקת is only after the verdict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבא's ruling fits only Reading 1, the גמרא adopts it. So according to רבי יוחנן, everyone agrees that before the verdict a person can back out. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue only about after the verdict.

keyTerms.meaning: Can't we learn from this? (a suggested conclusion)
Yes, learn it from this: the conclusion is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, before גמר דין everyone agrees a person can back out. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue only about after גמר דין.

phrases.english: Rather, can't we learn from this:
that the dispute is after the verdict?
Yes, learn it from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוחנן, the מחלוקת is only after גמר דין. Before it, everyone agrees he can back out.

steps.title: A question sent to רב נחמן בר יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא asks רב נחמן בר יעקב two things: when is the מחלוקת, and whom does the הלכה follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent to רב נחמן בר יעקב: Let our teacher teach us. Is the מחלוקת before the verdict or after the verdict? And whose words does the הלכה follow?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. A student sends his teacher a question asking for both the correct reading and the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question is the same one ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argued about in Step 7. The second question is new: in practice, do we rule like רבי מאיר or like חכמים?

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him, by letter or messenger
Let our teacher teach us: a polite way to ask a question
The practical ruling

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Nachman son of Rav Chisda sent
to Rav Nachman bar Yaakov:
Let our teacher teach us:
Is the dispute before the verdict
or is the dispute after the verdict?
And whose words does the halacha follow?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב: יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new exchange that asks the question from Step 7 again and adds a question about the practical הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the מחלוקת applies (before or after גמר דין), and whether the הלכה follows רבי מאיר or חכמים

steps.title: The dispute is after the verdict and the הלכה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יעקב answers that the מחלוקת is after גמר דין and the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: the מחלוקת is after the verdict, and the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יעקב answers both questions. This gives the final practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer matches רבי יוחנן as the גמרא concluded in Step 11. Since the הלכה follows חכמים, a person can back out before the verdict but not after it. That is exactly רבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי מאיר; they say he cannot back out

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: if someone accepted a relative or disqualified person, he can back out before גמר דין, but after גמר דין he cannot, following חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: once the verdict is given, a person cannot cancel it by backing out of what he agreed to.

phrases.english: He sent back to him:
The dispute is after the verdict,
and the halacha follows the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: לְאַחַר גְּמַר דִּין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is after גמר דין, and the הלכה follows חכמים: after the verdict he cannot back out.

steps.title: רב אשי's version of the question
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the question that was sent was different: is the מחלוקת about "אתן לך" or about "מחול לך"? And whom does the הלכה follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is what was sent: Is the argument about a case of "I will give you," or about a case of "it is forgiven to you"? And whose opinion is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different version of the question that was sent to רב נחמן בר יעקב. In his version, the question is not about before or after גמר דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 12–13, the question was about timing: before or after גמר דין. In רב אשי's version, the question is about the type of case. In "אתן לך", someone agrees to pay. In "מחול לך", someone agrees to drop his claim. The second half of the question, whom the הלכה follows, stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: "I will give you": a person agrees to pay
"It is forgiven to you": a person agrees to drop his claim
According to whose words?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is a second way of reporting the same letter from steps 12–13, with the question worded differently.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
This is what he sent to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן בר רב חסדא, sending to רב נחמן בר יעקב, the same two people as in step 12.

phrases.english: Is the dispute about "I will give you,"
or is the dispute about "It is forgiven to you"?
And the halakha is according to whose words?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָכִי שְׁלַח לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the question from step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of case the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים covers ("אתן לך" or "מחול לך"), and whom the הלכה follows

steps.title: The dispute is in "I will give you"; the הלכה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The reply: the מחלוקת is in the "אתן לך" case, and the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: The argument is about "I will give you," and the הלכה follows the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: In רב אשי's version, רב נחמן בר יעקב answers that the argument is in the "אתן לך" case. He also rules like חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer places the מחלוקת in the case where someone agrees to pay. That means the "מחול לך" case is not where they argue. The ruling itself is the same as in step 13: the הלכה follows חכמים. So both versions agree on the final ruling and differ only on what the question was about.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a written reply)
The Sages, who argue with רבי מאיר

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רב נחמן בר יעקב rules like חכמים. They differ only on the details of the question.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
The dispute is about "I will give you,"
and the halakha is according to the words of the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: בְּ״אֶתֵּן לָךְ״ מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is in the "אתן לך" case, and the הלכה follows חכמים

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version: a קנין before the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The previous exchange is how they learned it in סורא. In פומבדיתא they learned a different question, sent from רב's study hall to שמואל: if a קנין was made before גמר דין, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they learn it this way. In פומבדיתא they learn it this way: רב חנינא בר שלמיה said: They sent from רב's study hall to שמואל: Let our teacher teach us: if it is before גמר דין, but a קנין was made with him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא notes that the earlier exchange is the סורא version. Then it gives the פומבדיתא version, which is a different question sent to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9–11 already said that before גמר דין a person can back out. This question adds one detail: what if the parties made a formal קנין to lock in their agreement? The question asks whether the קנין makes the agreement binding even before the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The two great yeshivos of Bavel
רב's study hall
"Let our teacher teach us": a polite way to ask a question
They made a formal act of acquisition with him, a קנין

phrases.english: In Sura they teach it this way.
In Pumbedita they teach it this way:
Rav Ḥanina bar Shelemya says:
They sent from Rav's study hall to Shmuel:
Let our teacher teach us:

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי גְּמַר דִּין וְקָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ, מַאי?
phrases.english: Before the verdict, and they made an act of acquisition with him, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי. בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Labels the earlier exchange as the סורא version and gives the פומבדיתא version instead
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person can back out before גמר דין if a קנין was made

steps.title: שמואל: after a קנין, there is no backing out
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that after a קנין nothing can be undone, even before גמר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to them: After a קנין, there is nothing to say.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that once a קנין was made, the person cannot back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before גמר דין a person can usually back out. A קנין changes that, because it locks the agreement in place right away. So the קנין does what the final ruling would normally do.

keyTerms.meaning: A formal act that makes an agreement legally binding
There is nothing (no backing out)

steps.whatToRemember: Normally a person can back out before גמר דין. But once a קנין is made, he cannot back out at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a קנין makes an agreement to go to a certain judge binding, without waiting for the ruling.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
There is nothing after an act of acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: אֵין לְאַחַר קִנְיָין כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After a קנין, nobody can back out, even before גמר דין

steps.title: The משנה lists people who are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists people who are פסולין: one who plays with dice, one who lends with interest, those who race pigeons, and merchants of שביעית produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the people who are disqualified: one who plays dice, one who lends with interest, those who fly pigeons, and those who trade in שביעית produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It gives a list of people who are disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was choosing judges and backing out of that choice. Now the משנה moves to a new topic: who is not fit. Every person on the list does something wrong involving money.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are disqualified
One who plays with dice (for money)
One who lends with interest
Those who race or fly pigeons
Those who trade in produce of the Sabbatical year

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the disqualified ones:
one who plays with dice,
and one who lends with interest,
and those who fly pigeons,
and merchants of Sabbatical-Year produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַפְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dice players, lenders with interest, pigeon racers, and traders in שביעית produce are פסולין

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the name changed from gatherers to merchants
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that at first these people were called "gatherers of שביעית". Once the tax collectors became many, people went back to calling them "merchants of שביעית".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: At first they called them "gatherers of שביעית." When the tax collectors became many, they went back to calling them "merchants of שביעית."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a note about the name of the last group in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the name was "gatherers" (אוספי שביעית). Later, after the tax collectors increased, the name became "merchants" (סוחרי שביעית). The change in name signals a change in who is being described. The משנה does not explain why, and the גמרא will discuss it later.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatherers of Sabbatical-year produce
Oppressors; here, the tax collectors who forced people to pay
They went back to calling them

steps.whatToRemember: The list of פסולין ends with "merchants of שביעית". רבי שמעון tells us that this name replaced an earlier name, "gatherers".

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִילָּה הָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָן אוֹסְפֵי שְׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: Initially they would call them gatherers of Sabbatical-Year produce.
Once the tax collectors grew many,
they went back to calling them merchants of Sabbatical-Year produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: בַּתְּחִילָּה הָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a note about the name of the last item in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name changed from "gatherers of שביעית" to "merchants of שביעית" once the tax collectors increased

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the disqualification to those with no other job
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the people listed in the משנה are פסולין only when this is their only occupation. If they have another real job, they are כשרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When are they disqualified? When they have no job except this one. But if they have a job other than this one, they are fit to be witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי יהודה adding a limit to the list of פסולין from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה said dice players, lenders with interest, pigeon racers and שביעית merchants are פסולין. רבי יהודה narrows this: they are פסול only if this activity is their whole livelihood. Someone who also has a proper trade stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: When? It is used to limit when a rule applies
A trade or occupation
Fit, here meaning valid as witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהודה's 'other job' limit becomes important in step 26. There the גמרא quotes it to challenge רמי בר חמא, because a gambler with another trade is exactly where רמי בר חמא and רב ששת differ (step 25).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When?
phrases.notes: He is asking when the people listed in the משנה (step 18) are disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן אוּמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: When they have no occupation except this one,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהֶן אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הוּא –
phrases.english: but if they have an occupation other than this one –
they are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֵימָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the משנה's list of פסולין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed people are פסולין only when this is their sole occupation; with another trade they are כשרין.

steps.title: What is wrong with a dice player?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what wrong a dice player does that makes him פסול לעדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One who plays with dice, what is he doing wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why gambling with dice should disqualify a person. This sets up two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gambling does not look like plain theft, because both players agreed to play. So the גמרא wants to know what the actual problem is. The answer will decide which gamblers are פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: One who plays with dice, gambling for money
What is he doing (wrong)?

phrases.english: GEMARA: One who plays with dice,
what is he doing?
phrases.notes: He means: what wrong is he doing that would make him unfit to testify?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשַׂחֵק בְּקוּבְיָא, מַאי קָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the first item in the משנה's list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a dice player is disqualified from testimony

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: gambling is an אסמכתא, so winnings are not truly acquired
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says gambling is an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not make a קנין. So the winner is holding money that is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: Because it is an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not make a קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the question. The dice player is like a thief, because his winnings are not legally his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a promise made without full commitment, because the person is sure he will win. Since the loser never truly agreed to pay, the money does not legally pass to the winner. Taking it is a kind of גזל, and that disqualifies him.

keyTerms.meaning: A commitment made without full intent, relying on an outcome the person expects will not happen
Does not make a קנין; ownership does not transfer

steps.confusionAlert: רמי בר חמא is not saying gambling is just a waste of time. He is saying the money itself is not legally the winner's, so it is like stealing.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
Because it is an asmakhta,
phrases.notes: The gambler agrees to pay only because he is sure he will win, so he never truly means it.

phrases.english: and an asmakhta does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה אַסְמַכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gambling is an אסמכתא, which does not make a קנין, so the winner holds money that is like stolen money

steps.title: רב ששת: not an אסמכתא; the problem is no productive work
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת disagrees. Gambling is not an אסמכתא at all. The dice player is פסול because he is not involved in יישובו של עולם, meaning useful work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Anything like this is not an אסמכתא. Rather, he is disqualified because such people are not busy with building up the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a different answer to the same question. He rejects רמי בר חמא's reason and offers his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת holds that both gamblers know they might lose, so the money does pass to the winner and there is no theft. The problem is the gambler's way of life: he does no productive work. Such a person is not trusted as a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this
Building up the world; productive work that helps society

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא לָאו אַסְמַכְתָּא הִיא,
phrases.english: Anything like this is not an asmakhta,
rather, because they are not involved
in the settling of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: כֹּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא לָאו אַסְמַכְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's אסמכתא reason and gives a competing answer to step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gambling is a real transfer of money, but the gambler is פסול because he does no productive work

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case where רמי בר חמא and רב ששת would rule differently. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons disqualify an ordinary gambler. So the גמרא looks for a case where only one reason applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 22 and 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two explanations give different rulings

steps.title: The difference: a gambler who also learned another trade
steps.stepSummary: They differ about a gambler who has learned another occupation. For רב ששת he is כשר, since he does productive work. For רמי בר חמא he is still פסול, since his winnings are still like stolen money.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where he learned another trade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the difference is a gambler who also has a real job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's reason is about not working, so a gambler with a real trade is no longer פסול. רמי בר חמא's reason is about money not legally gained, and that stays true even if he has a job. This matches רבי יהודה's 'other job' limit in the משנה, which fits רב ששת's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Another trade or occupation

steps.whatToRemember: Dice player: רמי בר חמא says the problem is אסמכתא (winnings are like גזל), so he is פסול even with a job. רב ששת says the problem is no productive work, so he is כשר if he has another trade.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he learned another trade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּגְמַר אוּמָּנוּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is a gambler who has another occupation: כשר for רב ששת, פסול for רמי בר חמא

steps.title: The משנה's ruling from רבי יהודה seems to support רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה: gamblers are פסול only when they have no other job. This shows the reason is יישובו של עולם, which is a difficulty for רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה said, when are they פסול? Only when they have no job except this one. But if they have another job, they are כשר. So the reason of the משנה is יישובו של עולם, and that is a difficulty for רמי בר חמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה that seems to prove רב ששת right and רמי בר חמא wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 we learned that the two opinions differ about a gambler who has another job. רבי יהודה rules that such a gambler is כשר. That only makes sense if the problem is not doing useful work (רב ששת), not that the winnings are stolen money (רמי בר חמא).

keyTerms.meaning: A trade or occupation.
Apparently, this shows that...
It is a difficulty. The source contradicts the opinion.

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the debate from steps 22-25 into a real test against the משנה itself.

phrases.english: But we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said: When?
phrases.notes: He means: when are the dice players and the others listed in the משנה פסול?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן אוּמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הוּא;
phrases.english: When they have no occupation except this one;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהֶן אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הוּא –
phrases.english: but if they have an occupation other than this one,
they are fit to testify.
Apparently, the reason of the Mishnah
is because of settling the world.
phrases.notes: This is רב ששת's reason from step 23: the gambler does no useful work.

phrases.english: This is a difficulty for Rami bar Chama!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the practical difference from step 25 to test the two opinions against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's reason that gambling is an אסמכתא (stolen money).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה makes a gambler with another job כשר. If the winnings were stolen, a second job would not help, so the reason must be יישובו של עולם.

steps.title: A possible defense: the Sages disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out for רמי בר חמא: maybe the חכמים argue with רבי יהודה, and רמי בר חמא follows the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for רמי בר חמא, but phrases it as 'if you would say', which hints that it will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים of the משנה hold that all gamblers are פסול, even with another job, then רמי בר חמא can follow them. Then רבי יהודה's ruling would be only his own opinion and would not disprove רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. It brings up a possible answer, usually so that it can be pushed back.
They disagree.
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכי תימא' is not the גמרא's final answer. It is a suggestion that the גמרא is about to push back on.

phrases.english: And if you would say: the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of רמי בר חמא against the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinions: רבי יהודה is a minority view and the חכמים argue with him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's ruling speaks for the whole משנה, so רמי בר חמא is disproven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי יהודה is arguing, and רמי בר חמא follows the חכמים.

steps.title: Pushing back with רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to reject the defense by quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about every place where רבי יהודה says something in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say: every place where רבי יהודה said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject the defense from step 27 by bringing a general rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי. This is a setup line, and the rule itself finishes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is about to show that when רבי יהודה says 'אימתי' (when?), he is explaining the חכמים, not arguing with them. If so, the חכמים also hold that a gambler with another job is כשר, and the challenge to רמי בר חמא comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... Used to bring a source against what was just said.
Every place, a general rule for the whole משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Any place where Rabbi Yehuda said

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins objecting to the defense in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע בן לוי has a rule about how to read רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. The rule is completed in the next part of the daf.
